1.why: Deeper water has more weight pressing down above it, which increases fluid pressure.

wrong.a: Pressure increases with depth, not decreases.
wrong.d: Pressure builds up with depth, it does not drop.

2.why: ρ is the Greek letter rho, representing density in mass per unit volume.

3.why: High tides raise sea levels, causing water to overflow coastal barriers.

wrong.a: Sea levels rise during high tides.
wrong.b: Wind is not the main driver of tidal floods.

cover.title: Why coastal floods push so hard
cover.subtitle: High tides and rising seas push water onto city streets. Find out how water pressure builds up when sea levels rise.
cover.subject: Physics · Pressure
cover.fun_fact: Water pressure increases with depth because every extra meter of water adds weight above.
story.title: Water pushing against the city
story.lead: BMKG reported on maritime safety and coastal conditions [1]. Rising sea water covers roads and pushes against walls with heavy force [2].
story.image_caption: Coastal flooding in Jakarta during high tide
stat.1.label: relative density factor
stat.2.label: gravitational factor
stat.3.label: kPa pressure from 2 m of water depth
story.body_1: When ocean tides rise above normal levels, water spills over coastal defences and floods streets. This is known as a coastal flood or banjir rob [1]. As sea levels rise globally due to climate change, these coastal floods happen more often [2].
story.body_2: Water is heavy and fluid. When it piles up against seawalls or enters neighbourhoods, it exerts tremendous pressure on everything it touches. Understanding this pressure helps engineers design stronger barriers to protect coastal communities [3].
timeline.1.text: Tide starts rising along the Jakarta coastline.
timeline.2.text: Sea water overflows barriers onto coastal streets.
timeline.3.text: Water pressure tests seawalls and drainage systems.
physics.title: Hydrostatic water pressure
physics.body_1: Water pressure depends on how deep the water is, how dense the liquid is, and gravity. Deeper water pushes down with more force.
physics.body_2: We calculate this using the hydrostatic pressure equation. P is pressure, ρ is density, g is gravity, and h is depth.
physics.assumptions: We assume static water and uniform density throughout the depth.
table.note: Pressure increases directly with water depth.
graph.title: Water pressure at different depths
graph.1.label: 1 m
graph.2.label: 2 m
graph.3.label: 3 m
graph.note: Pressure doubles when water depth doubles from 1 m to 2 m.
physics.tip: Greater depth means higher pressure. Even shallow flood water exerts strong sideways force on walls.

lab.title: Water depth and container pressure
lab.step_1: Punch small holes at different heights in a plastic bottle and fill with water.
lab.step_2: Observe how far water squirts from holes at different depths.
lab.step_3: Measure the distance water squirts from bottom versus top holes.
lab.question: Which hole squirted water further and why?
